newsitem.title: USA: Boise posts another loss; office product unit net off.
newsitem.headline: Boise posts another loss; office product unit net off.

text.p: Boise Cascade Corp. Monday reported a loss for the third quarter, blaming flat sales, and predicted sluggish business until market conditions improve.
The company said it lost $1.7 million, or 24 cents a share, versus a profit of $118.5 million, or $1.83 a share, in the third quarter of 1995. Revenues were flat at $1.3 billion.
The third-quarter loss compared with an even bigger deficit of $17 million in the second quarter.
Boise said it expects its paper business to remain sluggish until market conditions improve, and said its building products unit will likely weaken seasonally in the fourth quarter.

It said the sale, which was announced in September, of its coated paper business, which includes a pulp and paper mill in Rumford, Maine, and 667,000 acres of timberland to the Mead Corp. for $650 million in cash, will boost future earnings. The sale is expected to be completed by year-end.
Boise Cascade's stock gained 37.5 cents to $33.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Separately, the company said its Boise Cascade Office Products Corp. unit posted lower earnings for the third quarter despite a 53 percent jump in sales to a record high.

The Itasca, Ill.-based distributor of office products said it earned $11.7 million, or 19 cents a share, in the third quarter on record revenues of $507 million. The results compared with year-ago earnings of $12.5 million, or 20 cents a share, on revenues of $332.0 million.
Boise Cascade Office's stock was off 50 cents at $19.125 on the NYSE.
